questions.name: Think (section 8.1): all points 4 cm from P
questions.s_figure: A point P with a circle of radius 4 cm drawn around it, and two points Q and R on the circle, each joined to P by a straight line marked 4 cm.

questions.q_figure: Five artwork pictures: two equal circles side by side and touching; a circle with a smaller circle inside it sharing its centre; three equal circles in a row, each overlapping the next; a mouse face made of a big circle with two ear circles, two small circles with dots for eyes, a dot for the nose and a short line for the mouth; and two lines crossing like an X with a small circle at the bottom end of each line.

questions.name: Construct 2: Wavy Wave (section 8.1)
questions.q_figure: Two shaded half circles on a horizontal central line, the left one above the line and the right one below it, each shaded with fine vertical lines.
questions.s_figure: The wave on a central line AB of 8 cm with the middle point X marked, the first half circle from A to X above the line and the second from X to B below it, both shaded with vertical lines.

questions.q_figure: A line AB of 8 cm with a point X on it and a half circle drawn above the line from A to X, with the compass opening and the length AX each marked with a question mark.
questions.s_figure: The half circle on AX with AX = 4 cm marked as its diameter and the radius of 2 cm marked from the middle of AX.
A wave drawn on a central line of a different length, with two equal half circles, one above the line and one below it.

questions.name: Construct 1: A Person (section 8.1)
questions.q_figure: A person drawn as a circle for the head, a short straight line below it for the neck, and below that a rectangle whose top edge is a curve dipping in the middle, with the neck line touching the lowest point of that curve.
questions.s_figure: The body of the person with its curved top drawn by a compass whose tip is placed above the body, from one top corner of the body to the other.
Two identical arcs on a central line, one above the line and one below it, each shorter than a half circle.

questions.name: Construct 3: Eyes (section 8.1)
questions.q_figure: Two identical eyes side by side, each an almond shape made of an upper curve and a lower curve meeting at two pointed ends, with a filled black circle in the middle.
questions.s_figure: One eye with two light horizontal guide lines through it and the two compass-tip points, A above the eye and B below it, marked.

questions.name: Naming by Corners: which is not a name
questions.q_figure: A square with corner S at the top left, P at the top right, Q at the bottom right and R at the bottom left.
questions.s_figure: The same square with an arrow path going round S, P, Q and R in turn and a dashed diagonal joining Q and S.

questions.q_figure: A dot grid with four tilted four-sided figures A, B, C and D whose corners lie on dots: A, B and C are diamonds of different widths and heights, and D is a small thin tilted rectangle.
questions.s_figure: Each of the four figures with the dots counted across and down along its sides, the counts equal on every side of A only.

questions.q_figure: A rectangle in the middle, about twice as wide as it is tall, with four equal small squares placed symmetrically around it, one near each corner and outside it, not touching it.
questions.s_figure: The same configuration on a dot grid, with each small square placed one dot diagonally away from its corner of the rectangle.

questions.name: Think (section 8.2): sides and angles from dots
questions.q_figure: A dot grid with four tilted four-sided figures A, B, C and D whose corners lie on dots: A, B and C are diamonds of different widths and heights, and D is a small thin tilted rectangle.
questions.s_figure: Figure A on the dot grid with the dots across and the dots down counted along each of its four sides, the same counts on every side and swapped at each turn.
A dot grid with three tilted squares and rectangles drawn with their corners on dots.
Rectangle ABCD with AB = CD = 4 cm and AD = BC = 6 cm and all four right angles marked.
Rectangle PQRS with PQ = SR = 10 cm and PS = QR = 2 cm and all four right angles marked.

questions.name: Construct Q3 (section 8.3)
questions.s_figure: A base with perpendiculars drawn at both of its ends, running side by side the same distance apart, with the right angles marked.

questions.name: Rectangle Exploration: table of XY lengths
questions.q_figure: Rectangle ABCD with AB = 7 cm and BC = 4 cm, a point X on side AD and a point Y on side BC joined by a dashed line, and an empty table with three columns headed Distance of X from A, Distance of Y from B and Length of XY.
questions.s_figure: The table filled with three rows: 5 mm, 3 cm, 7 cm 4 mm; 1 cm, 1 cm, 7 cm; 2 cm, 4 cm, 7 cm 3 mm.

questions.name: Rectangle Exploration: XY at equal distances
questions.q_figure: Rectangle ABCD with AB = 7 cm and BC = 4 cm, and a table with columns Distance of X from A, Distance of Y from B and Length of XY, whose first two columns are filled with 5 mm and 5 mm, 1 cm and 1 cm, 1 cm 5 mm and 1 cm 5 mm and whose last column is empty.
questions.s_figure: The table with the length of XY filled in as 7 cm in every row.

questions.name: Rectangle Exploration: XY and the shape ABYX
questions.q_figure: Rectangle ABCD with a point X on side AD and a point Y on side BC at the same distance from A and B, with the dashed line XY and the four-sided figure ABYX marked.
questions.s_figure: The figure ABYX with XY and AB marked as equal and its four right angles marked.

questions.name: Rectangle Exploration: the farthest distance
questions.q_figure: Rectangle ABCD with AB = 7 cm and BC = 4 cm and both diagonals AC and BD drawn.
questions.s_figure: The rectangle with X placed at A and Y at C, so that XY lies along the diagonal AC.

questions.name: Example 1: Breaking Rectangles into squares
questions.q_figure: A rectangle divided by two vertical lines into three equal squares side by side.
questions.s_figure: A rectangle of three equal squares, and a rough diagram of a rectangle ACDF split into two squares ABEF and BCDE with short strokes marking the equal sides.

questions.name: Breaking Rectangles: sides that cannot be split

questions.q_figure: A rectangle 8 cm long and 4 cm tall with a square inside it that touches the top and the bottom, drawn with a vertical line for each side of the square.
questions.s_figure: The rectangle with the inner square of side 4 cm and a gap of 2 cm marked on each side of the square.

questions.q_figure: Two staircase figures: three squares of side 4 cm rising to the right, each touching the next at one corner, and three squares of sides 7 cm, 5 cm and 3 cm from bottom to top, also touching corner to corner.
A large square made of small squares in a 4 by 4 pattern, most of them cut by a diagonal with one half shaded with fine parallel lines, and a plain larger square filling the bottom left corner.

questions.name: Construct 4: Square with a Hole (section 8.4)
questions.q_figure: A square with a circular hole drawn in the middle of it.
questions.s_figure: The square with both diagonals drawn and the circle drawn with its centre where the diagonals meet.

questions.q_figure: A large square divided into four equal squares by two middle lines, with a circle in the middle of each small square.
questions.s_figure: The same square with the diagonals of each small square drawn and each circle centred where they meet.

questions.q_figure: A square of side 8 cm with four arcs, one on each side, each going from one corner of its side to the other corner and bulging inwards.
questions.s_figure: The square with four small construction points marked outside it, one beyond the middle of each side, and the four inward arcs drawn from them.

questions.name: Explore (section 8.5): diagonal splitting a corner equally
questions.s_figure: A square with one diagonal drawn, dividing the corner at each end of the diagonal into two angles of 45°.

questions.name: Example 2: Rectangle with a 60° and 30° diagonal
questions.s_figure: Rectangle ABCD with the diagonal AC making 60° with AB and 30° with AD, and the right angle at D marked.
Rectangle ABCD with the diagonal AC making 50° with AB and 40° with AD.
The square ABCD with the diagonal AC making 45° with AB and 45° with AD.

questions.name: Example 3: Rectangle from a side and a diagonal
questions.s_figure: Rectangle ABCD with the base DC = 5 cm, the diagonal DB = 7 cm drawn and the right angles marked.
Rectangle PQRS with PQ = 4 cm and the diagonal QS = 8 cm drawn and the right angles marked.
Rectangle ABCD with AB = 3 cm and the diagonal BD = 7 cm drawn and the right angles marked.

questions.name: Example 4: Recreating the house figure
questions.q_figure: A house outline: a rectangle DBCE with base DE = 5 cm and vertical sides of 5 cm, a door 1 cm wide and 2 cm tall on the base, a roof with two sides AB and AC of 5 cm meeting at a top point A, and a curved arc from B to C dipping down inside the house.
questions.s_figure: The house with circles of radius 5 cm around B and around C crossing at the top point A, and the arc from B to C drawn with its centre at A.
A larger house like the first one with every border line 7 cm, a door on the base, a roof with two sides of 7 cm meeting at a top point A, and a curved arc from B to C.

Three drawings: a person with a circle for the head, a neck line and a square body; a wave of equal half circles above and below a central line; and a pair of matching almond-shaped eyes with filled pupils.
A four-sided figure ABDC with all four sides 5 cm and angles that are not right angles.
